  7|붉은 눈동자가 온순하게 깜빡인다. C급 레어 몬스터, 그 무시무시한 홉 고블린 대전사도 이런 표정을 지을 수 있구나.
  8|
  9|‘지금껏 왜 몰랐을까.’
 10|
 11|가벼운 의문과 함께 창날에 묻은 피를 털었다. 동시에.
 12|
 13|쿵.
 14|
 15|육중한 뭔가가 땅으로 떨어졌다. 물건의 정체를 확인한 대전사가 저도 모르게 주춤주춤 뒷걸음질 친다.
 16|
 17|그래, 그럴 만도 하지. 팔꿈치 아래로 오른팔이 싹둑 잘려 나갔으니.
 18|
 19|‘그래도 너는 좀 다를 줄 알았는데.’
 20|
 21|진가보법. 그래, 나는 바로 그 진가보법을 펼치며 놈의 품속으로 파고들었다. 대전사가 반사적으로 오른팔을 휘둘렀지만 이미 잘려 나간 그곳은 텅 비어 있었다.
 22|
 23|“벌써 잊었냐?”
 24|
 25|나는 대전사의 옆구리에 창날을 붙이고 동시에 위로 쳐올렸다. 공력을 머금은 창날이 딱딱한 피부와 근육을 갈라낸다.
 26|
 27|서걱-
 28|
 29|초록색 핏물과 함께 놈의 왼팔이 떨어져 나왔다.
 30|
 31|순식간에 양팔을 잃은 홉 고블린 대전사가 분노와 고통으로 뒤범벅된 고함을 내질렀다.
 32|
 33|- 크아아아악!
 34|
 35|하지만 방심은 금물이다. 양팔을 잃었지만 놈은 맨몸으로도 충분히 위협적인 존재니까.
 36|
 37|“어. 들어와.”
 38|
 39|말이 끝나기도 전에 거대한 신형이 달려들었다.
 40|
 41|캉! 캉! 캉!
 42|
 43|역시, 이 녀석은 육체 자체가 무기다. 괴물답게 인간을 뛰어넘은 원시적인 감각과 힘을 지니고 있다.
 44|
 45|쉭. 촤악.
 46|
 47|갈고리발톱이 팔뚝을 스쳤다. 살점이 한 움큼 뜯겨 나가고 피가 쏟아진다. 나는 동요하지 않고 정수리를 향해 내리 찍히는 발뒤꿈치를 막아 냈다.
 48|
 49|쿵. 까드득.
 50|
 51|내가 딛고 선 지면이 점점 꺼지기 시작한다.
 52|
 53|엄청난 힘. 이대로는 선 채로 파묻힐지도 모른다.
 54|
 55|‘공력이 없었다면, 말이지.’
 56|
 57|나는 단전의 모든 공력을 끌어 올렸다. 사지백해로 흘러 들어간 힘. 서서히 올라오는 창대에 놈의 눈동자가 흔들렸다.
 58|
 59|‘늦었어.’
 60|
 61|처음부터 온전한 상태였다면 모를까, 이미 양팔을 잃은 홉 고블린 대전사는 더 이상 내 상대가 되지 못한다.
 62|
 63|- 크르르.
 64|
 65|결국 놈이 먼저 물러났다. 그리고 그 시점에서 이미 승부는 갈린 거나 마찬가지였다.
 66|
 67|나는 멈추지 않고 창을 뻗어 냈다.
 68|
 69|‘진가창법 일 초식.’
 70|
 71|몸과 머릿속에 각인된 동작들이 빠르게 펼쳐졌다.
 72|
 73|찌른다. 벤다. 창대로 막고 때린다. 따로 보면 단순한 동작이지만 순서와 위치에 따라 무수한 조합이 탄생한다.
 74|
 75|그게 내가 정의 내린 무공(武功)이다.
 76|
 77|캉! 캉!
 78|
 79|쉭. 쉬쉬쉭!
 80|
 81|이 초식. 삼 초식. 사 초식…….
 82|
 83|강철만큼 단단하던 갈고리발톱이 잘려 나갔다. 한 걸음씩 물러날 때마다, 새로운 상처가 생기고 더 많은 피가 쏟아졌다.
 84|
 85|어느 순간 홉 고블린 대전사의 등이 벽면에 닿았다.
 86|
 87|“크르륵…….”
 88|
 89|C급 레어 몬스터. 도저히 상대할 수 없을 것 같던 이 괴물의 붉은 눈동자는 이미 전의를 상실한 지 오래였다.
 90|
 91|“가라, 이제.”
 92|
 93|푹.
 94|
 95|끄륵. 단말마와 함께 녹색 거체가 벽면을 타고 미끄러진다.
 96|
 97|그리고.
 98|
 99|띠링.

103|- [Lv.45 홉 고블린 대전사]를 처치했습니다!
104|
105|- 레벨 업!
106|
107|
108|
109|시스템 알림이 울렸다. 다시는 듣지도, 보지도 못할 거라고 생각했는데…….
110|
111|‘난데없이 시스템이라니.’
112|
113|하지만 혼란스러워하는 건 나만이 아니었다.
114|
115|“……진태경 씨?”
116|
117|어느새 제사장을 처리한 최 팀장의 동공이 지진 난 것처럼 흔들린다. 그가 나와 대전사의 시체를 번갈아 바라봤다.
118|
119|“당신…… 정체가 뭡니까?”
120|
121|그러게. 그거 나도 알고 싶다.
122|
123|허허, 허허허.
124|
125|
126|
127|* * *
128|
129|
130|
131|“레어 몬스터요?”
132|
133|공무원이 물고 있던 담배가 툭 떨어졌다.
134|
135|천생 공무원 체질로 보이는 그로서는 영 좋은 소식은 아니다. 아니나 다를까, 우리를 살펴보는 눈빛이 불안하기 짝이 없다.
136|
137|“며, 몇 급이요?”
138|
139|최 팀장이 피곤한 얼굴로 제사장의 지팡이를 흔들었다.
140|
141|쩔그럭.
142|
143|“C급 레어, 홉 고블린 제사장.”
144|
145|“C급?! 이런 씨…….”
146|
147|어, 욕 아껴 둬. 하나 더 있으니까.
148|
149|나는 지팡이처럼 짚고 있던 홉 고블린 대전사의 대검을 발로 찼다. 둔탁한 소리에 공무원이 고개를 돌린다.
150|
151|“그건?”
152|
153|“하나 받고 하나 더. C급 레어, 홉 고블린 대전사.”
154|
155|“중급 레어 몬스터가 둘? 겨우 E급 게이트에?”
156|
157|그의 반응을 이해한다. 이건 뭐, 말이 되는 수준이어야지.
158|
159|공무원은 한동안 우리와 장비를 번갈아 바라보다가 결국 슬픈 얼굴로 고개를 끄덕였다.
160|
161|“일단 상부에 연락하겠습니다.”
162|
163|“어이, 아저씨. 잠깐만.”
164|
165|어느새 정신을 차린 임꺽정이다. 내 부축을 받고 있는 그는 최소 뼈 다섯 군데가 부러지는 중상을 입었다.
166|
167|“힐러 불러 줘. 예쁜 언니로.”
168|
169|E급 트리오도 땅바닥에 털썩 주저앉았다.
170|
171|“포션도 줘! 포션! 좋은 걸로다가!”
172|
173|“에이 시발, 게이트 관리를 어떻게 한 거야!”
174|
175|“장비도 다 박살 나고, 어! 이거 다 어떡할 거야!”
176|
177|어떡하긴 뭘 어떡해. 정부 쪽에서 다 보상해 주겠지.
178|
179|이 경우 게이트에서 소비된 모든 물품과 치료비 및 보상금까지 지급해 주는 법률이 버젓이 존재한다.
180|
181|저건 그러니까, 조금이라도 더 뜯어내려는 쇼인 거다.
182|
183|‘쯧쯧. 아무리 그래도 그렇지. 사람들 눈이 있는데.’
184|
185|그때 옆에서 따가운 시선이 느껴졌다.
186|
187|“……태경 씨.”
188|
189|최 팀장이다.
190|
191|“뭐 하십니까?”
192|
193|그는 혼란스러운 눈빛으로 나를 바라보고 있었다. 정확히 말하면 단검을 쥔 내 손을.
194|
195|그그극.
196|
197|공력이 실린 단검에 죽죽 그어진 7년 차 가죽 갑옷은 더 이상 사용할 수 없을 만큼 망가져 있었다.
198|
199|“…….”
200|
201|“…….”
202|
203|“최 팀장님.”
204|
205|나는 땅이 꺼져라 한숨을 내쉬었다.
206|
207|“홉 고블린 대전사. 정말 강한 놈이더군요. 목숨은 건졌지만 갖고 있는 모든 장비가 망가져 버렸어요.”
208|
209|“…….”
210|
211|“7년 동안 절 지켜 준 갑옷, 이제는 창까지.”
212|
213|“창은 멀쩡해 보이는…….”
214|
215|그 순간, 나는 한쪽 발로 창의 중앙을 지그시 눌렀다.
216|
217|세 자릿수 근력 스탯의 위엄에 철창이 엿가락처럼 휘어진다.
218|
219|“멀쩡하다고요? 이게요?”
220|
221|“…….”
222|
223|최 팀장은 입을 다물었다.
224|
225|
226|
227|* * *
228|
229|
230|
231|최 팀장은 책임자 자격으로 파견된 공무원들에게 불려 갔고, 나머지 넷은 치료를 받기 위해 앰뷸런스로 옮겨졌다.
232|
233|나는 퀴퀴한 휴게실 대신 넓고 쾌적한 사무실에 홀로 남았다. 막상 그 순간이 다가오자 심장이 쿵쾅거리며 뛰었다.
234|
235|‘사, 상태창?’
236|
237|반신반의하는 그 부름에, 시스템이 응답했다.
238|
239|띠링.
240|
241|
242|
243|상태창
244|

247|[Lv.33 진태경]

250|

259|근력 : 120  체력 : 125

269|- 동기화가 완료된 상태입니다. 칭호와 명성에 변화가 생깁니다.
270|
271|
272|
273|“시발. 진짜 뜨네.”
274|
275|잠시 넋 놓고 상태창을 바라보던 나는 뭔가 이상한 점을 깨달았다.
276|
277|‘상태창이…… 바뀌었다?’
278|
279|일단 가장 먼저 눈에 띈 건 0으로 리셋된 명성과 사라진 칭호 두 가지다. 마지막 줄을 읽어 보니 대충 짐작 가는 부분이 있었다.
280|
281|‘무림이 아니라서?’
282|
283|내가 쌓은 500의 명성은 모두 무림인으로서 쌓은 것이다. 그리고 이번에 사라진 칭호, [명가의 자제]도 같은 맥락에서 이해할 수 있다.
284|
285|‘하긴, 나는 여기서 명문가 자제도 아니고, 잠룡 같은 건 더더욱 아니니까.’
286|
287|굳이 칭호를 받는다면 서민층 자제나 잠룡 대신 지렁이. 뭐 그런 수준일 게 뻔하다.
288|
289|“다른 건 얼마나 바뀌었을라나?”
290|
291|나는 십여 분간 시스템의 모든 기능을 한 번씩 켰다 끄며 시험해 봤지만 달라진 건 상태창뿐이었다.
292|
293|아니, 하나 더 있긴 했다. 바로 퀘스트창이다.
294|
295|띠링.
296|
297|
298|
299|퀘스트
300|
301|
302|
303|[배신자]
304|
305|당신은 배신자의 정체를 알아냈습니다. 본대에 합류하여 배신자가 있음을 알리고 전투를 승리로 이끄십시오!
306|
307|
308|
309|등급 : 절정
310|
311|제한 : 진태경
312|
313|임무 : 배신자 처단 (미완료)
314|
315| 전투 승리 (미완료)
316|
317|보상 : 막대한 경험치와 명성
318|
319| 귀중한 철궤
320|
321|실패 : 사망
322|
323|
324|
325|
326|
327|곽준과 암살자들을 해치우고 받은 연계 퀘스트다. 나는 머릿속이 복잡해지는 것을 느꼈다.
328|
329|‘다시 돌아가라는 건가? 무림으로?’
330|
331|이제는 안다. 내가 겪은 무림은 환상도, 게임도 아니라는 것을. 매우 비현실적인 이야기지만 무림은 아마도…….
332|
333|끼익.
334|
335|갑작스러운 소리에 고개를 돌렸다. 최 팀장이 문 앞에 서 있었다.
336|
337|“가시죠, 태경 씨.”
338|
339|대충 이야기가 마무리된 모양이다. 나는 생각을 접고 일어났다.
340|
341|“다른 분들은…….”
342|
343|“지금쯤이면 병원으로 가고 있을 겁니다. 일주일 정도 입원해야 한다고 해서요. 걱정하실 필요 없습니다.”
344|
345|딱히 걱정은 하지 않는다. 전투 계열 헌터의 튼튼한 신체에 포션, 치료 마법까지 받았으니 곧 자리를 털고 일어날 것이다.
346|
347|그리고…….
348|
349|“어떻게 됐나요?”
350|
351|“며칠 내로 다시 연락이 올 겁니다. 아마 태경 씨한테도 조사관이 갈 거고요.”
352|
353|조사관이라.
354|
355|다시 마주치고 싶지 않은 부류다. 하지만 내가 원한 대답은 이게 아니었다. 그래서 다시 물었다.
356|
357|“다른 건요?”
358|
359|“흠.”
360|
361|최 팀장이 묘한 표정으로 나를 바라봤다. 마치 신기한 동물을 쳐다보는 것 같은 눈초리였다.
362|
363|‘사실대로 말했을까?’
364|
365|내 힘을 드러내고 싶지 않다. 왜 현실에서 시스템이 보이는지, 무림과의 연관성도 잘 모르는 이 시점에서는 더더욱.
366|
367|F급 헌터가 C급 레어 몬스터를 혼자서 잡았다는 것은 유례없는 일이다. 낭중지추. 튀어나온 송곳과는 반대되는 인생을 살아온 나로서는 조심스러울 수밖에.
368|
369|그래서 그에게 부탁했다.
370|
371|
372|
373|‘저에 관해서는 비밀로 해 주실 수 있을까요?’
374|
375|
376|

Creak.

[P132]
I turned at the sudden sound. Team Leader Choi stood in the doorway.

[P133]
“Let’s go, Mr. Taekyung.”

[P134]
It seemed the discussion had wrapped up. I put the thought aside and rose.

[P135]
“The others…?”

[P136]
“They should be on their way to the hospital by now. They’ll need to stay there for about a week. You don’t need to worry.”

[P137]
I wasn’t particularly worried. Combat-type Hunters had sturdy bodies, and they’d received potions and healing magic. They would be back on their feet soon enough.

[P138]
And…

[P139]
“How did it go?”

[P140]
“They’ll contact us again within a few days. An investigator will probably visit you as well.”

[P141]
An investigator.

[P142]
Not the sort of person I ever wanted to deal with again. But that wasn’t the answer I wanted, so I asked once more.

[P143]
“What about the other matter?”

[P144]
“Hmm.”

[P145]
Team Leader Choi regarded me with a strange expression, like he was examining some fascinating animal.

[P146]
*Did he tell them the truth?*

[P147]
I didn’t want my strength exposed. Especially not now, when I still had no idea why the System had appeared in reality or how any of this was connected to Murim.

[P148]
An F-rank Hunter single-handedly killing a C-rank Rare Monster was unprecedented. A needle in a bag would eventually poke through, but I’d spent my whole life being the opposite of that—never standing out at all. I couldn’t help being cautious.

[P149]
So I had asked him:

[P150]
“Could you keep what happened with me a secret?”

[P151]
It must have been a difficult request from Team Leader Choi’s perspective. I was asking him to give a false statement for someone he’d only just met.

[P152]
“Mr. Jin Taekyung.”

[P153]
“Yes.”

[P154]
His grave voice made my heart sink.

[P155]
Then he said, “Let’s get something to eat.”

[P156]
“What?”

[P157]
“Look.”

[P158]
Team Leader Choi held out his wrist. A gleaming Magic Gem digital watch showed two in the afternoon.

[P159]
“It’s an N Company model carved from a solid C-rank Magic Gem. It’s enchanted with reinforcement magic, so in an emergency, you can even use it as a shield—”

[P160]
*So that’s what he meant.*

[P161]
“…Let’s go.”

[P162]
The man was impossible to read.

[P163]
“Let’s get some meat. Do you like Hanwoo?[^1]”

[P164]
“Hanwoo?”

[P165]
“Yes. Highest grade.”

[P166]
And he was rich too.

[P167]
“I can never get enough of it.”

[P168]
This wasn’t just any beef. It was Hanwoo. Top-grade Hanwoo, at that.

[P169]
System or whatever—first, I needed to fill my empty stomach.

[P170]
[^1]: Hanwoo is beef from Korean native cattle, prized as premium meat.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

* dropped image, attitude, or timing

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

  2|

  7|붉은 눈동자가 온순하게 깜빡인다. C급 레어 몬스터, 그 무시무시한 홉 고블린 대전사도 이런 표정을 지을 수 있구나.

  9|‘지금껏 왜 몰랐을까.’

 11|가벼운 의문과 함께 창날에 묻은 피를 털었다. 동시에.
 12|
 13|쿵.
 14|
 15|육중한 뭔가가 땅으로 떨어졌다. 물건의 정체를 확인한 대전사가 저도 모르게 주춤주춤 뒷걸음질 친다.

 21|진가보법. 그래, 나는 바로 그 진가보법을 펼치며 놈의 품속으로 파고들었다. 대전사가 반사적으로 오른팔을 휘둘렀지만 이미 잘려 나간 그곳은 텅 비어 있었다.
 22|

 25|나는 대전사의 옆구리에 창날을 붙이고 동시에 위로 쳐올렸다. 공력을 머금은 창날이 딱딱한 피부와 근육을 갈라낸다.
 26|
 27|서걱-
 28|
 29|초록색 핏물과 함께 놈의 왼팔이 떨어져 나왔다.
 30|
 31|순식간에 양팔을 잃은 홉 고블린 대전사가 분노와 고통으로 뒤범벅된 고함을 내질렀다.
 32|
 33|- 크아아아악!

 35|하지만 방심은 금물이다. 양팔을 잃었지만 놈은 맨몸으로도 충분히 위협적인 존재니까.
 36|
 37|“어. 들어와.”
 38|
 39|말이 끝나기도 전에 거대한 신형이 달려들었다.
 40|
 41|캉! 캉! 캉!
 42|
 43|역시, 이 녀석은 육체 자체가 무기다. 괴물답게 인간을 뛰어넘은 원시적인 감각과 힘을 지니고 있다.
 44|
 45|쉭. 촤악.
 46|
 47|갈고리발톱이 팔뚝을 스쳤다. 살점이 한 움큼 뜯겨 나가고 피가 쏟아진다. 나는 동요하지 않고 정수리를 향해 내리 찍히는 발뒤꿈치를 막아 냈다.
 48|
 49|쿵. 까드득.
 50|
 51|내가 딛고 선 지면이 점점 꺼지기 시작한다.
 52|
 53|엄청난 힘. 이대로는 선 채로 파묻힐지도 모른다.
 54|
 55|‘공력이 없었다면, 말이지.’
 56|
 57|나는 단전의 모든 공력을 끌어 올렸다. 사지백해로 흘러 들어간 힘. 서서히 올라오는 창대에 놈의 눈동자가 흔들렸다.
 58|
 59|‘늦었어.’
 60|
 61|처음부터 온전한 상태였다면 모를까, 이미 양팔을 잃은 홉 고블린 대전사는 더 이상 내 상대가 되지 못한다.
 62|
 63|- 크르르.
 64|
 65|결국 놈이 먼저 물러났다. 그리고 그 시점에서 이미 승부는 갈린 거나 마찬가지였다.
 66|

 68|
 69|‘진가창법 일 초식.’
 70|
 71|몸과 머릿속에 각인된 동작들이 빠르게 펼쳐졌다.
 72|
 73|찌른다. 벤다. 창대로 막고 때린다. 따로 보면 단순한 동작이지만 순서와 위치에 따라 무수한 조합이 탄생한다.
 74|
 75|그게 내가 정의 내린 무공(武功)이다.
 76|
 77|캉! 캉!
 78|
 79|쉭. 쉬쉬쉭!
 80|
 81|이 초식. 삼 초식. 사 초식…….
 82|
 83|강철만큼 단단하던 갈고리발톱이 잘려 나갔다. 한 걸음씩 물러날 때마다, 새로운 상처가 생기고 더 많은 피가 쏟아졌다.
 84|
 85|어느 순간 홉 고블린 대전사의 등이 벽면에 닿았다.
 86|
 87|“크르륵…….”
 88|
 89|C급 레어 몬스터. 도저히 상대할 수 없을 것 같던 이 괴물의 붉은 눈동자는 이미 전의를 상실한 지 오래였다.
 90|
 91|“가라, 이제.”
 92|
 93|푹.
 94|
 95|끄륵. 단말마와 함께 녹색 거체가 벽면을 타고 미끄러진다.
 96|

103|- [Lv.45 홉 고블린 대전사]를 처치했습니다!
104|
105|- 레벨 업!
106|
107|
108|
109|시스템 알림이 울렸다. 다시는 듣지도, 보지도 못할 거라고 생각했는데…….
110|
111|‘난데없이 시스템이라니.’
112|
113|하지만 혼란스러워하는 건 나만이 아니었다.
114|
115|“……진태경 씨?”
116|
117|어느새 제사장을 처리한 최 팀장의 동공이 지진 난 것처럼 흔들린다. 그가 나와 대전사의 시체를 번갈아 바라봤다.
118|
119|“당신…… 정체가 뭡니까?”
120|
121|그러게. 그거 나도 알고 싶다.
122|
123|허허, 허허허.
124|
125|
126|

128|
129|
130|
131|“레어 몬스터요?”
132|
133|공무원이 물고 있던 담배가 툭 떨어졌다.
134|
135|천생 공무원 체질로 보이는 그로서는 영 좋은 소식은 아니다. 아니나 다를까, 우리를 살펴보는 눈빛이 불안하기 짝이 없다.
136|
137|“며, 몇 급이요?”
138|
139|최 팀장이 피곤한 얼굴로 제사장의 지팡이를 흔들었다.
140|
141|쩔그럭.
142|
143|“C급 레어, 홉 고블린 제사장.”
144|
145|“C급?! 이런 씨…….”
146|
147|어, 욕 아껴 둬. 하나 더 있으니까.
148|
149|나는 지팡이처럼 짚고 있던 홉 고블린 대전사의 대검을 발로 찼다. 둔탁한 소리에 공무원이 고개를 돌린다.
150|
151|“그건?”
152|
153|“하나 받고 하나 더. C급 레어, 홉 고블린 대전사.”
154|
155|“중급 레어 몬스터가 둘? 겨우 E급 게이트에?”
156|
157|그의 반응을 이해한다. 이건 뭐, 말이 되는 수준이어야지.
158|
159|공무원은 한동안 우리와 장비를 번갈아 바라보다가 결국 슬픈 얼굴로 고개를 끄덕였다.
160|
161|“일단 상부에 연락하겠습니다.”
162|
163|“어이, 아저씨. 잠깐만.”
164|
165|어느새 정신을 차린 임꺽정이다. 내 부축을 받고 있는 그는 최소 뼈 다섯 군데가 부러지는 중상을 입었다.
166|
167|“힐러 불러 줘. 예쁜 언니로.”
168|
169|E급 트리오도 땅바닥에 털썩 주저앉았다.

171|“포션도 줘! 포션! 좋은 걸로다가!”

173|“에이 시발, 게이트 관리를 어떻게 한 거야!”

175|“장비도 다 박살 나고, 어! 이거 다 어떡할 거야!”
176|
177|어떡하긴 뭘 어떡해. 정부 쪽에서 다 보상해 주겠지.
178|
179|이 경우 게이트에서 소비된 모든 물품과 치료비 및 보상금까지 지급해 주는 법률이 버젓이 존재한다.
180|
181|저건 그러니까, 조금이라도 더 뜯어내려는 쇼인 거다.
182|
183|‘쯧쯧. 아무리 그래도 그렇지. 사람들 눈이 있는데.’

185|그때 옆에서 따가운 시선이 느껴졌다.

190|
191|“뭐 하십니까?”
192|
193|그는 혼란스러운 눈빛으로 나를 바라보고 있었다. 정확히 말하면 단검을 쥔 내 손을.
194|
195|그그극.
196|
197|공력이 실린 단검에 죽죽 그어진 7년 차 가죽 갑옷은 더 이상 사용할 수 없을 만큼 망가져 있었다.
198|
199|“…….”
200|
201|“…….”
202|
203|“최 팀장님.”
204|
205|나는 땅이 꺼져라 한숨을 내쉬었다.
206|
207|“홉 고블린 대전사. 정말 강한 놈이더군요. 목숨은 건졌지만 갖고 있는 모든 장비가 망가져 버렸어요.”
208|
209|“…….”
210|
211|“7년 동안 절 지켜 준 갑옷, 이제는 창까지.”
212|

*Why hadn’t I noticed before?*

[P5]
With that passing thought, I shook the blood from my spearhead. At the same moment—

[P6]
Thud.

[P7]
Something heavy hit the ground. The Great Warrior saw what it was and instinctively shuffled backward.

[P8]
Well, fair enough. Its right arm had been severed cleanly below the elbow.

[P9]
*I thought you’d be a little different.*

[P10]
The Jin Family’s Manoeuvre Technique. Yeah, I’d used it to slip inside the creature’s reach. The Great Warrior reflexively swung its right arm, but there was nothing left to swing.

[P11]
“Forgot already?”

[P12]
I pressed the spearhead against the Great Warrior’s side and ripped it upward. The blade, charged with internal energy, split its tough hide and muscle.

[P13]
Slash—

[P14]
Its left arm fell away in a spray of green blood.

[P15]
Both arms gone in an instant, the Hobgoblin Great Warrior let out a roar of rage and pain.

[P16]
—Kuwaaaaaargh!

[P17]
But I couldn’t let my guard down. Even without arms, it was still more than dangerous enough with its body alone.

[P18]
“Yeah. Come at me.”

[P19]
Before I’d even finished speaking, its massive frame charged.

[P20]
Clang! Clang! Clang!

[P21]
As expected, this thing’s entire body was a weapon. Like the monster it was, it possessed primal senses and strength that far surpassed a human’s.

[P22]
Swish. Slash.

[P23]
A hooked claw grazed my forearm. A chunk of flesh tore away, and blood poured out. Without flinching, I blocked the heel descending toward the crown of my head.

[P24]
Thud. Crunch.

[P25]
The ground beneath my feet began to sink.

[P26]
Incredible strength. At this rate, I might be buried standing up.

[P27]
*If I didn’t have internal energy, that is.*

[P28]
I drew up every last bit of internal energy in my dantian. Power flooded through every limb. As my spear shaft slowly rose, the Great Warrior’s eyes wavered.

[P29]
*Too late.*

[P30]
It might have been different if the creature had been whole, but after losing both arms, the Hobgoblin Great Warrior was no longer a match for me.

[P31]
—Grrr.

[P32]
In the end, it was the first to back off. By then, the fight was as good as over.

[P33]
I pressed forward and thrust my spear.

[P34]
*Jin Family’s Spear Technique. First form.*

[P35]
The movements engraved into my body and mind unfolded in rapid succession.

[P36]
Thrust. Cut. Block with the shaft, then strike. Each movement was simple on its own, but changing the order and target created countless combinations.

[P37]
That was my definition of martial arts.

[P38]
Clang! Clang!

[P39]
Swish. Swish-swish-swish!

[P40]
Second form. Third form. Fourth…

[P41]
The hooked claws, once as hard as steel, were sliced away. With every step the creature retreated, another wound opened and more blood spilled.

[P42]
Before long, the Hobgoblin Great Warrior’s back struck the wall.

[P43]
“Grrrk…”

[P44]
A C-rank Rare Monster. A creature that had once seemed impossible to fight. But the will to resist had long since vanished from its red eyes.

[P45]
“Time to go.”

[P46]
Shunk.

[P47]
Ghk. With a final death rattle, the hulking green body slid down the wall.

[P48]
And then—

[P49]
Ding.

[P50]
> **System**
>
> You have defeated Lv. 45 Hobgoblin Great Warrior!
>
> Level Up!

[P51]
The System notification rang out. I’d thought I would never hear or see one again…

[P52]
*The System, out of nowhere?*

[P53]
But I wasn’t the only one confused.

[P54]
“…Mr. Jin Taekyung?”

[P55]
Team Leader Choi had already dealt with the Priest. His pupils shook as if an earthquake had struck while he looked back and forth between me and the Great Warrior’s corpse.

[P56]
“What… are you?”

[P57]
Good question. I wanted to know too.

[P58]
Heh heh. Heh heh heh.

[P59]
* * *

[P60]
“A Rare Monster?”

[P61]
The cigarette dropped from the government official’s mouth.

[P62]
He looked like a born civil servant, so this couldn’t have been welcome news. Sure enough, his gaze darted anxiously over us.

[P63]
“W-what rank?”

[P64]
Team Leader Choi wearily shook the Priest’s staff.

[P65]
Clank.

[P66]
“C-rank Rare. Hobgoblin Priest.”

[P67]
“C-rank?! For fuck’s—”

[P68]
Hey, save the swearing. There’s one more.

[P69]
I kicked the Hobgoblin Great Warrior’s greatsword, which I’d been using as a walking stick. The official turned at the dull clang.

[P70]
“And that?”

[P71]
“Buy one, get one more. C-rank Rare. Hobgoblin Great Warrior.”

[P72]
“Two mid-grade Rare Monsters? In an E-rank Gate?”

[P73]
I understood his reaction. This was too absurd to make any sense.

[P74]
The official spent a while looking back and forth between us and the equipment before finally nodding with a miserable expression.

[P75]
“I’ll contact my superiors first.”

[P76]
“Hey, mister. Hold on.”

[P77]
Im Kkeokjeong had regained consciousness at some point. I was supporting him, and he’d suffered severe injuries, including at least five broken bones.

[P78]
“Call us a healer. A pretty one.”

[P79]
The E-rank trio collapsed onto the ground as well.

[P80]
“And potions! Potions! Give us the good stuff!”

[P81]
“For fuck’s sake, how did you people even manage this Gate?!”

[P82]
“All our gear’s smashed too! Huh? What are you going to do about this?!”

[P83]
What did they think he was going to do? The government would compensate them for everything.

[P84]
There was an actual law requiring it to cover every item consumed inside the Gate, along with medical expenses and compensation.

[P85]
In other words, this was all a show to squeeze out a little more.

[P86]
*Tsk, tsk. Even so, people are watching.*

[P87]
That was when I felt a piercing stare from beside me.

[P88]
“…Mr. Taekyung.”

[P89]
It was Team Leader Choi.

[P90]
“What are you doing?”

[P91]
He stared at me in confusion. More precisely, at the hand holding my dagger.

[P92]
Grrrk.

[P93]
The dagger, charged with internal energy, carved long gashes through my seven-year-old leather armor until it was too badly damaged to use.

[P94]
“…”

[P95]
“…”

[P96]
“Team Leader Choi.”

[P97]
I heaved a sigh deep enough to sink the ground.

[P98]
“That Hobgoblin Great Warrior was incredibly strong. I escaped with my life, but every piece of equipment I owned was destroyed.”

[P99]
“…”

[P100]
“The armor that protected me for seven years. Now even my spear…”

[P101]
“The spear looks perfectly—”

[P102]
At that moment, I planted one foot on the middle of the spear and slowly pressed down.

[P103]
Before the majesty of my three-digit Strength stat, the iron spear bent like taffy.

[P104]
“Perfectly fine? This does?”

[P105]
“…”

[P106]
Team Leader Choi shut his mouth.

[P107]
* * *

[P108]
As the person in charge, Team Leader Choi was called away by the dispatched officials, while the other four were taken to an ambulance for treatment.

[P109]
Instead of the musty break room, I was left alone in a spacious, comfortable office. Now that the moment had finally arrived, my heart began to pound.

[P110]
*St-Status Window?*

[P111]
The System answered my doubtful summons.

[P112]
Ding.

[P113]
> **System**
>
> **Status Window**
>
> **Lv. 33 Jin Taekyung**
>
> **Job:** First Rate Martial Artist
>
> **Fame:** 0
>
> **Titles:** 2 (Title effects active)
>
> - Novice Trainee (Training speed +10%)
> - Gambler (Combat-related stats +10% in one-on-one matches)
>
> **Strength:** 120  **Stamina:** 125
>
> **Agility:** 121  **Intelligence:** 20
>
> **Charm:** 20  **Internal Energy:** 15 years
>
> **Remaining Points:** 30
>
> Synchronization is complete. Titles and Fame have changed.

[P114]
“Fuck. It really appeared.”

[P115]
I stared blankly at the Status Window for a moment before noticing something strange.

[P116]
*The Status Window… changed?*

[P117]
The first things that jumped out were my Fame, which had been reset to zero, and the two missing Titles. The final line gave me a rough idea why.

[P118]
*Because this isn’t Murim?*

[P119]
All five hundred Fame I’d accumulated had been earned as a martial artist in Murim. The missing Title, *Scion of a Prestigious Family*, made sense for the same reason.

[P120]
*Well, I’m not the son of some prestigious family here. And I’m sure as hell no Hidden Dragon.*

[P121]
If I earned a Title here, it would probably be something like *Scion of the Common Folk*. Or *Earthworm* instead of *Hidden Dragon*.

[P122]
“What else changed?”

[P123]
For the next ten minutes or so, I opened, closed, and tested every System function. The Status Window was the only thing that had changed.

[P124]
No. There was one more.

[P125]
The Quest Window.

[P126]
Ding.

[P127]
> **System**
>
> **Quest**
>
> **Traitor**
>
> You have discovered the traitor’s identity. Rejoin the main force, warn them of the traitor, and lead the battle to victory!
>
> **Grade:** Peak
>
> **Restriction:** Jin Taekyung
>
> **Mission:** Eliminate the traitor (Incomplete)
>
> Win the battle (Incomplete)
>
> **Reward:** Vast EXP and Fame
>
> Valuable iron chest
>
> **Failure:** Death

[P128]
It was the Chain Quest I’d received after defeating Gwak Jun and the assassins. My thoughts grew tangled.

[P129]
*Does it want me to go back? To Murim?*

[P130]
I knew now. The Murim I’d experienced wasn’t an illusion or a game. As wildly unrealistic as it sounded, Murim was probably…

[P131]
Creak.

[P132]
I turned at the sudden sound. Team Leader Choi stood in the doorway.

[P133]
“Let’s go, Mr. Taekyung.”

[P134]
It seemed the discussion had wrapped up. I put the thought aside and rose.

[P135]
“The others…?”

[P136]
“They should be on their way to the hospital by now. They’ll need to stay there for about a week. You don’t need to worry.”

[P137]
I wasn’t particularly worried. Combat-type Hunters had sturdy bodies, and they’d received potions and healing magic. They would be back on their feet soon enough.

[P138]
And…

[P139]
“How did it go?”

[P140]
“They’ll contact us again within a few days. An investigator will probably visit you as well.”

[P141]
An investigator.

[P142]
Not the sort of person I ever wanted to deal with again. But that wasn’t the answer I wanted, so I asked once more.

[P143]
“What about the other matter?”

[P144]
“Hmm.”

[P145]
Team Leader Choi regarded me with a strange expression, like he was examining some fascinating animal.

[P146]
*Did he tell them the truth?*

[P147]
I didn’t want my strength exposed. Especially not now, when I still had no idea why the System had appeared in reality or how any of this was connected to Murim.

[P148]
An F-rank Hunter single-handedly killing a C-rank Rare Monster was unprecedented. A needle in a bag would eventually poke through, but I’d spent my whole life being the opposite of that—never standing out at all. I couldn’t help being cautious.

[P149]
So I had asked him:

[P150]
“Could you keep what happened with me a secret?”

[P151]
It must have been a difficult request from Team Leader Choi’s perspective. I was asking him to give a false statement for someone he’d only just met.

[P152]
“Mr. Jin Taekyung.”

[P153]
“Yes.”

[P154]
His grave voice made my heart sink.

[P155]
Then he said, “Let’s get something to eat.”

[P156]
“What?”

[P157]
“Look.”

[P158]
Team Leader Choi held out his wrist. A gleaming Magic Gem digital watch showed two in the afternoon.

[P159]
“It’s an N Company model carved from a solid C-rank Magic Gem. It’s enchanted with reinforcement magic, so in an emergency, you can even use it as a shield—”

[P160]
*So that’s what he meant.*

[P161]
“…Let’s go.”

[P162]
The man was impossible to read.

[P163]
“Let’s get some meat. Do you like Hanwoo?[^1]”

[P164]
“Hanwoo?”

[P165]
“Yes. Highest grade.”

[P166]
And he was rich too.

[P167]
“I can never get enough of it.”

[P168]
This wasn’t just any beef. It was Hanwoo. Top-grade Hanwoo, at that.

[P169]
System or whatever—first, I needed to fill my empty stomach.

[P170]
[^1]: Hanwoo is beef from Korean native cattle, prized as premium meat.
